opus.why: A multi-hour migration of 14 modules (javax to jakarta, Hibernate 6, security rewrite, Kafka retry) where every step must compile and pass tests. This is long-horizon agentic coding, which Opus at xhigh handles well.

fable.why: Multi-hour 14-module Spring Boot 2.7→3.3 migration with security config rewrite, Hibernate 6, and custom Kafka retry; large-scale refactoring gated by compile/tests. Opus is built for this; xhigh for the long agentic horizon. Guardrails (module-by-module, green tests, ask when unsure) keep it below Fable territory.

opus.why: A distributed-systems redesign with delivery guarantees (exactly-once effect, priorities, DLQ, replay), real tradeoffs between Kafka, RabbitMQ and Postgres at their volume, then a rewrite behind a flag. Architecture judgment drives the quality here.

fable.why: Core of the task is architecture: delivery-guarantee semantics (exactly-once effect, idempotency, priority starvation, dedup, DLQ, replay), a real Kafka/RabbitMQ/Postgres tradeoff at stated volumes, then a flagged rewrite. Subtle correctness reasoning where a weaker design silently loses messages; Fable at default high.

opus.why: Deep multi-source research: checking each claim's source, sample size and whether headlines misread it, across several countries, ending in a finished document. This is Fable's strength.

fable.why: Multistep deep research across countries and source types, carried through to a finished document, with per-claim verification of whether studies actually support headlines and flagging weak evidence. That critical-reading judgment is where lesser models accept claims at face value; Fable high per the research guidance.

opus.why: Overnight orchestration. Spawn subagents in batches of 6, retry up to 2 times, keep scratch in one folder, collect a table. The logic is procedural and well specified, and the creative work happens in the subagents. Sonnet at high is reliable enough.

fable.why: Overnight orchestration of 38 beats × prompter/judge with retry logic, strict batch-of-6 concurrency, scratch-dir rules, and an accurate final state table. Per-step reasoning is simple but the horizon is long and bookkeeping must not drift; Opus xhigh for reliable long-running agentic execution. Creative quality lives in the subagents, not here.

opus.why: A brand book rebuilt from scratch: competitor research, positioning, tone of voice, visual rules, image prompts. Brand judgment and copy the audience reads are where a quality drop shows most.

fable.why: Full brandbook rewrite from scratch after rebrand: competitor research, positioning, tone-of-voice with do/don't examples, visual rules, image-gen prompts. Brand and visual judgment plus audience-facing final copy are exactly where quality drops show most; Fable high.

opus.why: A zero-downtime migration of 900GB of prod data from MySQL to Postgres. It covers type-mapping traps, CDC, cutover and rollback, finding every MySQL-specific query, and a runbook. Mistakes are costly and the edge cases are subtle.

fable.why: Zero-downtime 900GB MySQL→Postgres migration: type-mapping traps (unsigned, zero dates, ENUM, ON UPDATE, JSON fulltext), CDC dual-write/backfill design, cutover and rollback plan, plus a hunt for every mysql-ism in raw SQL and a runbook. High-stakes data architecture where a missed edge case corrupts prod; Fable high.

opus.why: A strangler migration of about 180 AngularJS components to React and TS, with subagents per module plus review and merge. Long-running multi-agent coding with architecture decisions.

fable.why: Strangler migration of ~180 AngularJS components to React+TS with shared infra first, subagent delegation per module, review/merge, no UX changes, weekly reports. Large-scale refactoring with multi-agent coordination over a long horizon is Opus's target workload; xhigh for the duration. Pattern is well-established, so Fable not required.

opus.why: Deep research across papers, docs, community tests and pricing, ending in a decision matrix and a recommended stack with citations. This is multistep research carried through to a finished analysis.

fable.why: Deep research across papers, model docs, community benchmarks and pricing, synthesized into a decision matrix and recommended stack with fallback, fully cited and date-flagged. Multistep research carried through to a decision document with visual/production judgment; Fable high, matching rare-hard-03.

opus.why: Continues the modulith split: coordinate one subagent per bounded context, break cyclic dependencies, run the full test suite after each merge and protect contracts between contexts. Long-horizon agentic coding.

fable.why: Continues the modulith split: execute the agreed 5-phase plan with one subagent per bounded context, coordinate, run full test suite after each merge, stop on inter-context contract breaks. Long-horizon multi-agent refactoring execution with the design already settled; Opus xhigh.
